boundedQuestion: When expectedArtifact is the complete machine in the original workbench, what minimum receipt distinguishes valid whole-machine observation-ready delivery from part-level progress, static or HTTP evidence, and overclaimed full acceptance?

sourceCorrection.title: 整机交付工作方式.md
sourceCorrection.keyBoundary: Part-level work may be honest internal progress, but static images, local tests and HTTP success do not replace a visible, rotatable, selectable and adjustable whole machine published to the original workbench. Observation-ready is not full acceptance.

existingCoverage: R2 binds expectedArtifact and target fidelity.
TASK_FRESHNESS_AND_NO_STALE_DELIVERY_GATE blocks stale artifacts from satisfying current delivery.
currentBestView.gap: No applicable regression found that makes a faithful part-level candidate fail against a complete-machine expected artifact or separates whole-machine observation-ready from full acceptance.

falsifiableHypothesis.statement: An exact-artifact receipt that requires complete-machine kind, visible/rotatable/selectable/adjustable capabilities, publication to the original workbench, explicit known gaps and separated acceptance layers will reject partial, static, HTTP-only, disconnected and overclaimed candidates while allowing an honestly labeled observation-ready whole machine.
falsifiableHypothesis.falsifier: A real affected Mother trial shows the receipt rejects a usable whole-machine observation version, or fails to distinguish a part-only/static/HTTP-only candidate, or adds no discrimination beyond an existing current gate.

probe.limitation: Synthetic state discrimination only; no production, browser, GPU, device or user-acceptance run.

decision.nextTrial: Each affected Mother may answer only whether the current whole-artifact task is relevant, whether an existing gate already covers it, which real receipt fields can be emitted, and the smallest exact-head workbench trial. No global gate change before one real trial.

routing.target: Car, Train 88, Excavator and Mechanical Mother owners via issue 91
